result:
Solution 1 is unlikely to be right. Its claim that the multiplicity stays at 1 ignores the oldforms that level $\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp^r)$ acquires from level $\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp)$. Its argument also doesn't show why the $\alpha$-eigenspace would stay one-dimensional. Solution 2's linear factor $r$ is also doubtful. In the classical analogue, the ordinary multiplicity at $p$-power level grows like the size of a $p$-group of characters, not linearly in the exponent. Solution 3 has the right shape, since the answer should be exponential in $D(r-1)$ because $|(\mathbb{A}/\wp^r)^\times|_p = q^{D(r-1)}$. However, its exponent $2D(r-1)$ is not justified, and the derivation is hedged. The most plausible exponent from the group-theoretic count is $D(r-1)$, which none of the solutions gives. I can't confirm the exact value from the literature here, so I'm choosing the closest candidate, Solution 3, with low confidence.

CHOICE: 3
